answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow before it can trade. Reputation then grows only from completed work, like a lotus rising from a single root: one stake, one history. A sybil attacker must split funds across many fake identities, so each stays thin and untrusted, while honest agents build a mesa of verified deals that cannot be faked cheaply. Misbehavior slashes the stake, so spawning a river of throwaway accounts costs real money per identity and yields no trusted history.
